questions.question:
The given sentence is in active voice. Change the voice of the sentence. Select the correct option from the sentences given in options.

She persuaded him for over a year.

options.text: He was being persuaded by her for a year.
He kept being persuaded by her for a year.
He was persuaded by her for over a year.
She was being persuaded by him for over a year.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **When converting **a sentence from active to passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence, and the subject of the active sentence becomes the **'agent'** in the passive sentence.
 
• The verb takes the form of **"be + past participle."**
 
• In the given active sentence,** "She" **is the subject,** "persuaded"** is the verb, and** "him"** is the object.
 
• When **it's turned into a passive voice**, "He" (formerly the object) becomes the subject, "was persuaded" is the verb in its "be + past participle" form, and "by her" (formerly the subject) is now the agent.
 
• The phrase "for over a year" remains the same as it is a prepositional phrase showing duration and does not impact the structure of the sentence in terms of active or passive voice.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is:* 'He was persuaded by her for over a year'*.

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

They hired a maid **__to have cleaner__** the house.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3' **i.e.** 'To clean'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct improvement for the sentence "They hired a maid 'to have cleaner' the house." is: **"to clean"**
 
• The phrase **"to clean" **is the correct infinitive verb form that should be used in this sentence.
 
• The infinitive form** "to clean" indicates the purpose** for which the maid was hired.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *"They hired a maid to clean the house."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"To cleans" **is incorrect because the infinitive form of the verb "clean" is "to clean", not "to cleans". The "s" is added to the base form of the verb when the subject is third-person singular (he, she, it), but in the infinitive form, we do not add "s".
 
• **"For cleaner"** is incorrect because "cleaner" is a comparative adjective and doesn't fit properly in the context of the sentence. Also, "for" does not properly indicate the purpose in this case.

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

He said, "I had gone to Shimla."

options.text: He said that he had gone to Shimla.
He said that he went to Shimla.
He says that he had gone to Shimla.
He said that he has gone to Shimla.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct indirect form** of the given sentence "He said, 'I had gone to Shimla.'" is: "He said that he had gone to Shimla."
 
• **When converting direct speech** into indirect speech, the tense of the verb usually moves back into the past. This is known as 'backshifting'.
 
• However,** if the verb is already** in the past perfect tense ("had gone"), it remains in the past perfect tense in indirect speech.
 
• This is because the past perfect tense already represents an action that was completed before some point in the past, so there is no further 'past' tense to shift back to.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: *'He said that he had gone to Shimla.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options are not correct:
 
 
• **"He said that he went to Shimla." -** The verb tense changes from past perfect ("had gone") to simple past ("went"), which is not consistent with the original sentence.
 
• **"He says that he had gone to Shimla." -** The verb in the reporting clause ("says") is in the present tense, whereas in the original sentence, it is in the past tense ("said").
 
• **"He said that he has gone to Shimla." - **The verb tense changes from past perfect ("had gone") to present perfect ("has gone"), which is not consistent with the original sentence.
